title: Vicky Kaushal Has Blocked 18 Months of His Life for One Role. Nobody Else Exists.
excerpt: The Love and War star is about to disappear into a six-month physical transformation to become Parashurama. Shraddha Kapoor may join him. Bollywood's most ambitious mythological epic starts now.
body:
The most in-demand leading man in Hindi cinema just told every producer in Mumbai the same thing: don't call me for 18 months. I'm busy becoming a god.

Vicky Kaushal has blocked his entire calendar — from this month through December 2027 — exclusively for Mahavatar, the mythological epic in which he'll play Chiranjeevi Parashurama, the immortal warrior-sage and sixth avatar of Vishnu. Directed by Amar Kaushik (the man who made Stree and Stree 2 the most profitable horror franchise in Indian history) and produced by Dinesh Vijan under Maddock Films, Mahavatar is being positioned as the studio's most ambitious production ever.

And they mean it. This isn't a four-month shoot squeezed between brand commitments. This is total immersion.

Six Months of Prep Before a Single Frame

Starting this June, Kaushal will enter a rigorous six-month preparatory phase that reads more like military training than film prep. The programme includes a radical physical transformation — the kind of bulk-up that mythological spectacle demands — alongside intensive acting workshops designed by Kaushik himself.

"The prep is going on for 6-7 months. We have worked on the set design, weapon design, how every character would look. The scripting is done. Yet, we need more time." — Amar Kaushik

The director, who spoke to Bollywood Hungama about the project's scale, made it clear that every element — from Parashurama's iconic axe (the Parashu) to the world-building around ancient India — is being crafted from scratch. No shortcuts. No recycled VFX templates.

Once filming begins in January 2027, Kaushal will shoot exclusively on Mahavatar until the project wraps, likely by the end of 2027. No other film. No side projects. Just Parashurama.

Shraddha Kapoor May Complete the Picture

The casting buzz doesn't stop with Vicky. Shraddha Kapoor has emerged as the frontrunner for the female lead, and if the deal closes, it would mark the first time these two share screen space. The pairing makes a certain kind of sense: Shraddha's connection to the Maddock universe through the Stree franchise gives her an insider's understanding of Kaushik's visual language, and her star power matches the scale of the production.

Earlier reports had Deepika Padukone in discussions for the same role, but the makers have reportedly shifted their focus to Shraddha, who is currently finishing Eetha with Laxman Utekar.

Love and War First, Then War

Before he disappears into Parashurama, Vicky has one last commitment to honour: Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love and War, where he stars alongside Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt. Bhansali is racing to wrap a crucial 50-day schedule that started in May 2026, with a targeted release on Republic Day 2027. Kaushal is expected to finish his portions by the end of June — just in time to begin the Mahavatar prep.

The timeline is razor-thin. From Bhansali's opulent period drama to Kaushik's mythological warrior epic, Kaushal is essentially moving from one of Indian cinema's most demanding directors to another, with zero breathing room.

What Parashurama Means

For the uninitiated: Parashurama is one of the seven Chiranjeevis — the immortals of Hindu mythology. Born Ramabhadra of the Bhargava clan, he earned his name after receiving Lord Shiva's divine axe and leading the Devas to victory against the Asuras. He was Bheeshma's guru, Dronacharya's teacher, and Karna's mentor. In the Kalki mythology, he is the one who will appear at the end of Kali Yuga to train Vishnu's final avatar.

In other words: this isn't a role. It's a civilisational responsibility. And Kaushal is treating it like one.

What This Means for the Industry

The 18-month commitment signals a larger shift in Bollywood. The era of actors juggling four films simultaneously is fading. The biggest stars — Ranbir with Animal, Ranveer with his upcoming Pralay — are increasingly choosing singular, career-defining projects over volume. Kaushal's decision is the most extreme version of this trend yet.

Mahavatar was originally slated for Christmas 2026 but has been pushed to 2027, with Independence Day weekend emerging as the likely release window. That puts it in potential competition with Maddock's own Stree 3 — a scheduling puzzle the studio will need to solve.

For now, though, the picture is clear: Vicky Kaushal is about to vanish from public life. When he returns, he'll be carrying an axe.
